title: Trans-Caspia
subtitle: The Sealed Provinces of the Czar
summary: Michael Myers Shoemaker, an American from Cincinnati, travelled in the summer of 1894 through the Caucasus and the Russian provinces of Central Asia, which few foreigners were then allowed to enter. The book is written as a diary. With a companion, “B.”, he went from Berlin and St. Petersburg over the Dariel Pass to Tiflis, then to the oil fields of Baku, across the Caspian, and by the Trans-Caspian railway to Bokhara and Samarkand. By tarantass he went on to Tashkend, Kokand, Marghilan, and Osh, and then on horseback over the mountains into Chinese territory, where he fell ill and turned back. He came home by the railway and the Caspian, Trebizond, the cholera quarantine at Sinope, and Constantinople, where the book ends with a chapter on the city. It has fifty-three photographs.
